summary: This PR changes the default generic type parameters of `Factory`/`createFactory` from `any` to `Env`/`string`, and adds an explicit return type annotation to `createMiddleware`. This is a type-only fix intended to make middleware created via `factory.createMiddleware()` produce a correctly narrowed route schema instead of `any`, with accompanying test updates to verify the type behavior.

findings.rationale: Changing default type parameters from `any` to `Env`/`string` is a type-level breaking change: code that previously relied on `any` propagation (e.g., using `Factory` or `createFactory()` without explicit generics and expecting permissive typing across variables/params) may now fail to compile due to stricter inference, since `any` disables type-checking while `Env`/`string` do not.
findings.suggestedCheck: Run the full test suite and type-check across the codebase (and check downstream consumers/examples) to confirm no existing usages of `createFactory()`/`new Factory()` without explicit type args now fail to compile due to the narrower defaults.

findings.rationale: Only a single new type-level test was added for createMiddleware; other combinations (e.g., middleware with Input generics, or factory created with explicit Env/P) that exercise the changed default types are not covered.
findings.suggestedCheck: Confirm test coverage includes createMiddleware usage with an explicit Env/Input as well as the default case, to catch regressions in type narrowing.
